blockers.quote: Keep going. Past every language you could ever read. Past writing.
blockers.why: Ten years of nights is ~3,650 years lived, setting the timeline back to ~1624 BCE. Human writing originated c. 3400–3100 BCE (over 5,000 years ago), so asserting that walking 3,500 years back reaches 'Past writing' is an unsourced and inaccurate real-world claim without a row in claims.md.
blockers.fix: needs a source, or cut 'Past writing': 'Keep going. Past every language you could ever read.'

suggestions.quote: A student plugs in the night before the exam and sits it with a decade of revision; by Friday the exam board bans sleeping the night before.
suggestions.fix: A student plugs in the night before the exam and sits it with a year of revision; by Friday the exam board bans sleeping the night before.

suggestions.quote: and a head holds the new by rubbing out the old: a year of new, every night, and last night out here never stood a chance.
suggestions.fix: and a head holds the new by rubbing out the old (c13): a year of new, every night, and last night out here never stood a chance.

suggestions.quote: Out there a close friend takes more than 200 hours (c23). In here, that's twelve minutes of her evening.
suggestions.fix: Out there a close friend takes more than 200 hours (c23). In here, that's about twelve minutes of her evening.

keep.quote: your sleeping brain already replays the day fast, six to seven times in rats (c10), but a dream runs at real speed, lucid dreamers counting to ten take as long as awake (c11).
People dropped 31 metres into a net later judged their own fall 36% longer than other people's; a moment is as long as the memory it leaves (c18).
Night one hundred and twenty-three: you've lived longer than anyone whose life has ever been verified, Jeanne Calment, 122 years and 164 days (c27), and you're still paying rent on the same flat.
